title: Convergence of stationary distributions for a class of zero-range processes and its application to a wealth distribution model with debt
abstract: Understanding how macroscopic wealth distributions emerge from microscopic transaction rules among agents is a central problem in econophysics. While many traditional models restrict agents' wealth to non-negative values, debt is an essential feature of realistic economic systems. In this paper, we introduce a stochastic transaction mechanism into the agent-based model with a central-bank-mediated collective debt limit, as studied in [14]. In our model, each agent probabilistically determines whether to transfer a coin, depending on their current asset or debt level. From a probabilistic perspective, the resulting system can be formulated as a zero-range process with $\mathbb{Z}$-valued site occupation numbers, where negative values represent debt. We prove that, under an appropriate scaling, the wealth distribution in the stationary state converges to either a two-sided Gamma distribution or a Gamma distribution, depending on the asymptotic behavior of the function governing coin transfers. Our results rigorously identify these previously unconsidered limiting distributions and provide a mathematical framework for understanding how stochastic monetary exchanges give rise to macroscopic wealth distributions.
summary: This paper provides a rigorous mathematical framework for understanding wealth distribution in economies with debt by modeling it as a zero-range process. It proves that the stationary state converges to a predictable Gamma-type distribution, determined by the underlying transaction rules. This bridges statistical mechanics theory with complex economic modeling.
main_problem: The paper addresses how macroscopic wealth distributions and economic inequality emerge from microscopic, stochastic transaction rules, particularly when debt is allowed.
main_result: The stationary wealth distribution converges to either a two-sided Gamma distribution or a standard Gamma distribution, depending on the asymptotic behavior of the coin transfer function.
method: The analysis uses techniques from the theory of zero-range processes, involving the study of stationary measures, local limit theorems, and convergence in the thermodynamic limit.
model_or_system: The model is an agent-based system of wealth exchange formulated as a zero-range process on a lattice, generalized to allow negative site occupation numbers to represent debt, constrained by a central bank's total debt limit.
key_observables: The stationary wealth distribution $\mu_{K,L}^N(\xi)$, and its scaled limit $\mu_{\kappa,r}$.
important_parameters: Total wealth ($K$), total debt limit ($L$), the function governing coin transfers ($g(k)$), and the scaling parameters ($\kappa, r$).
main_assumptions: The process is assumed to be irreducible and the transition probability must be symmetric; convergence relies on specific asymptotic conditions on $g(k)$.
figures_summary: Figure 1 numerically compares simulated wealth distributions to the derived theoretical density $\mu_{\kappa,r}$ for two distinct cases determined by the relationship between $g_+$ and $g_-$.
paper_structure: The paper first establishes the existence of the stationary distribution for the zero-range process with debt. It then proceeds to prove the convergence of this distribution in the thermodynamic limit ($N 	o \infty$) using advanced limit theorems, culminating in the identification of the limiting Gamma distributions.
why_interesting: While focused on econophysics, the mathematical machinery—analyzing convergence in the thermodynamic limit for interacting particle systems (zero-range processes)—is highly relevant to non-equilibrium statistical mechanics and the study of interacting quantum many-body systems.
